newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures trapped in consolidative mode.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures trapped in consolidative mode.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were in a consolidative mode in late dealings on Friday as traders saw little reason for fresh buying or selling to emerge.
"There's no sign for now that Bund futures are going to break out of their sideways trend," said one Munich dealer, who looked for September futures to stay between 102.60 and 103.00.
"Buyers are now relatively well-invested in the market and potential sellers do not see enough fear in the market to put on fresh short positions," the trader said.
At 1435 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were up 26 basis points at 102.97.
The benchmark 10-year 6.00 percent cash Bund due July 2007 was bid at 103.39 for a yield of 5.54 percent compared with the closing price on Thursday at 103.18.
Deadlers said the market has reversed some of its losses sustained on Thursday when the September futures contract was overpowered by resistance.

They said the break on Friday to the session high at 102.98 broke through the tough level of 102.92/93 and could provide the market with fresh buying interest at the outset of dealings next week. But some said a breakdown would find support at 102.50 as bears sought to reach 102.00 to begin a turnaround.
The late German gains came after U.S. debt prices fell on profit-taking after U.S. producer price date met expectations and showed little sign of inflation.
Traders said the spread against 10-year Treasuries was steady at about 80 basis points and also steady against French and Italian debt.

The market generally ignored German Finance Minister Theo Waigel repeating again that the Bonn government would meet the three percent deficit criterion in 1997 to qualify for European monetary union.
